summary.text: Kyle Waterman is the Democratic candidate for Montana State Senate District 4 in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Republican Amy Regier for a seat with no incumbent.
An executive director from Kalispell who has been elected to the city council, Waterman has run for the state Senate in two earlier elections.

paragraphs.text: Kyle Waterman was born in Helena, Montana, and earned a bachelor’s degree from Evergreen State College.

In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, Waterman said he has more than 20 years of nonprofit management experience, including as a founding executive director of Friends of Ebey’s and as a senior development officer at Intermountain Children’s Services in the Flathead.
He said he was elected to the Kalispell City Council in 2018 and served on the Flathead County Health Board.
Waterman was the Democratic nominee for Montana State Senate District 2 in 2020, losing to Carl Glimm, and for Senate District 4 in 2022, losing to John Fuller.
He advanced from an uncontested Democratic primary for District 4 on June 2, 2026.

In his 2026 survey responses, Waterman listed his campaign messages as keeping Kalispell Kalispell, investing in local solutions and keeping water clean, and named funding for mental health services as a policy priority.
